--- title: "[Multinomial]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Multinomial logistic family for unordered categorical responses. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/multinomial.py#L31-L525){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python Multinomial(n_categories) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `Multinomial` models a categorical response with `K` unordered levels — for example, a choice among several unranked options — using a baseline-category logit model. Unlike `OrderedCategorical`, no assumption is made about the ordering of categories or a shared direction of covariate effects: each non-reference category `k` gets its own intercept `alpha_k` and its own loading coefficient `beta_k` that rescales the shared linear predictor `eta`, so different categories can respond differently (even in sign) to the same covariate effect. The final category `K` is fixed as the reference, with `alpha_K = 0` and `beta_K = 0`. Use this family when the response is nominal (has no natural order) with more than two levels; for binary outcomes use `Binomial`, and for ordinal outcomes use `OrderedCategorical`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n_categories]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of response categories `K` (must be `>= 2`). Responses passed to `GAM.fit()` should be integer-coded `1, 2, ..., K`, with category `K` as the reference. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} Category probabilities are obtained from a softmax over per-category logits built from the shared linear predictor `eta`: $$ P(Y = k \mid \eta) = \frac{\exp(\alpha_k + \beta_k \eta)} {\sum_{j=1}^{K} \exp(\alpha_j + \beta_j \eta)}, \qquad \alpha_K = \beta_K = 0. $$ As with `OrderedCategorical`, this loss does not fit the standard GLM deviance framework: `link` and `link_inverse` are the identity on `eta`, and a custom `irls_update` drives P-IRLS while an inner maximum-likelihood step (`_update_params`) re-estimates the per-category intercepts `alpha` and loadings `beta` at each iteration. The reported deviance is $-2$ times the multinomial log-likelihood of the observed categories under the fitted probabilities, $$ D(y, \hat P) = -2 \sum_{i} \log \hat P(Y_i = y_i \mid \eta_i). $$ ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAM to a three-level unordered categorical response: ::: {#1d80110a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = np.linspace(-3, 3, n) eta = np.sin(x) alphas = np.array([0.0, 0.5]) betas = np.array([1.0, -1.5]) logits = np.column_stack( [alphas[0] + betas[0] * eta, alphas[1] + betas[1] * eta, np.zeros(n)] ) probs = np.exp(logits) / np.exp(logits).sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) y = np.array([rng.choice([1, 2, 3], p=probs[i]) for i in range(n)], dtype=float) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAM("y ~ s(x)", family=wk.Multinomial(n_categories=3)) model.fit(data, method="REML") print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: Multinomial(K=3) Observations: 300 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err z value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) -0.0013 0.0231 -0.057 0.9545 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x) 5.39 6 87.175 1.169e-16 Total EDF: 6.39 Deviance: 534.0030 Null dev: 4154.4084 Dev. expl: 87.1% GCV score: 1.858347 Scale est: 1.000000 AIC: 546.79 BIC: 570.46 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
category_intercepts Fitted per-category intercepts `alpha_1, ..., alpha_{K-1}`.
category_loadings Fitted per-category loading coefficients `beta_1, ..., beta_{K-1}`.
n_categories Number of response categories `K`.
scale_known Whether the dispersion/scale parameter is fixed rather than estimated.
### [category_intercepts]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Fitted per-category intercepts `alpha_1, ..., alpha_{K-1}`. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [category_intercepts]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [category_loadings]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Fitted per-category loading coefficients `beta_1, ..., beta_{K-1}`. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [category_loadings]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [n_categories]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Number of response categories `K`. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [n_categories]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [scale_known]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the dispersion/scale parameter is fixed rather than estimated. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [scale_known]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}

### [deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Total multinomial deviance, implementing the family-specific `deviance` for ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/multinomial.py#L347-L390){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python deviance(y, mu, *, weights=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `Multinomial`. Computes $-2$ times the multinomial log-likelihood of the observed categories `y` under the fitted category probabilities implied by the linear predictor `eta = mu`: $$ D(y, \hat P) = -2 \sum_{i=1}^{n} \log \hat P(Y_i = y_i \mid \eta_i). $$ Returns `float(len(y))` as a placeholder if the family has not yet been fitted. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed categories, coded `1, 2, ..., K`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor `eta` (this family uses the identity link, so `mu` and `eta` coincide). [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Accepted for interface compatibility; does not currently affect the computed deviance. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total deviance. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Initialize category parameters and the starting linear predictor. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/multinomial.py#L501-L522){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific `initialize` for `Multinomial`: estimates starting intercepts `alpha` (from empirical log-odds relative to the reference category) and loadings `beta` (set to `1`) via `_init_params`, then returns a starting linear predictor of all zeros for the outer P-IRLS loop to refine. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed categories, coded `1, 2, ..., K`, used to compute starting intercepts. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Initial linear predictor `eta`, an array of zeros with the same shape as `y`. ::: ### [irls_update()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the P-IRLS working response and weights, implementing the family-specific ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/multinomial.py#L275-L345){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python irls_update(y, mu, eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} update for `Multinomial`. Overrides the default GLM IRLS step: because the multinomial deviance is not a standard exponential-family deviance in `eta`, this method first re-estimates the per-category intercepts `alpha` and loadings `beta` by maximum likelihood (via `_update_params`), initializing them on the first call (via `_init_params`). It then computes, for each observation `i` with observed category `k = y_i - 1` and fitted probabilities `p = P(Y_i = \cdot \mid \eta_i)`, the gradient and negative curvature of the multinomial log-likelihood with respect to `eta_i`: $$ \frac{\partial \ell_i}{\partial \eta_i} = \sum_{j=1}^{K-1} \beta_j \left( \mathbb{1}[j = k] - p_j \right), \qquad -\frac{\partial^2 \ell_i}{\partial \eta_i^2} = \sum_{j=1}^{K-1} \beta_j^2 p_j (1 - p_j) - 2 \sum_{j < l} \beta_j \beta_l p_j p_l. $$ The working weight `W` is the (clipped) negative curvature, and the working response is the Newton step `z = eta + grad / W`; both feed into the outer P-IRLS smoothing loop. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed categories, coded `1, 2, ..., K`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Unused; present for interface compatibility with other families. [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current linear predictor values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[NDArray, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The working response `z` and working weights `W`, both of shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Identity link, implementing the family-specific `link` for `Multinomial`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/multinomial.py#L196-L213){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Because `mu` here already represents the shared linear predictor `eta` fed into the per-category softmax (rather than a mean response on the natural scale), the link is the identity: $g(\mu) = \mu$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The input `mu`, unchanged. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Derivative of the identity link, implementing the family-specific version for ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/multinomial.py#L235-L251){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_derivative(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `Multinomial`. Since `link` is the identity, $g'(\mu) = 1$ everywhere. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values (only used to determine output shape). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of ones with the same shape as `mu`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Identity inverse link, implementing the family-specific `link_inverse` for ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/multinomial.py#L215-L233){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_inverse(eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `Multinomial`. Complements `link`: since `eta` is passed straight through to `_category_probs` for the softmax computation, the inverse link is also the identity, $g^{-1}(\eta) = \eta$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The input `eta`, unchanged. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Multinomial log-likelihood, implementing the family-specific version for `Multinomial`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/multinomial.py#L423-L448){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python log_likelihood(y, mu, scale, *, weights=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Recovers the log-likelihood from `deviance` via $\ell = -D / 2$, since `deviance` is defined as $-2$ times the log-likelihood. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed categories, coded `1, 2, ..., K`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor `eta`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Unused; present for interface compatibility with other families (the multinomial scale parameter is fixed, see `scale_known`). [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Forwarded to `deviance`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total log-likelihood of `y` under the fitted model. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Draw random responses from the fitted category probabilities, implementing the ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/multinomial.py#L463-L499){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simulate(mu, scale, rng) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} family-specific `simulate` for `Multinomial`. For each observation, computes the category probabilities from the linear predictor `eta = mu` via `_category_probs` and draws one category from `{1, ..., K}` according to those probabilities using `rng.choice`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor `eta` at which to simulate. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Unused; present for interface compatibility with other families. [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [object]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A random number generator exposing a `choice(a, p=...)` method (e.g. a NumPy `Generator`). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated categories, coded `1, 2, ..., K`, one per row of `mu`. ::: #### Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [RuntimeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called before the family has been fitted. ::: ### [unit_deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Per-observation deviance contributions, implementing the family-specific version for ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/multinomial.py#L392-L421){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python unit_deviance(y, mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `Multinomial`. For each observation `i`, returns $-2 \log \hat P(Y_i = y_i \mid \eta_i)$, the per-observation contribution to `deviance`. Returns an array of ones if the family has not yet been fitted. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed categories, coded `1, 2, ..., K`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor `eta` (this family uses the identity link). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of shape `(n,)` with the deviance contribution of each observation; these sum to the value returned by `deviance`. ::: ### [variance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Constant variance function, implementing the family-specific `variance` for ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/multinomial.py#L253-L273){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python variance(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `Multinomial`. The multinomial log-likelihood does not follow the mean-variance relationship used by standard GLM families; the working weights used by P-IRLS are instead derived directly from the curvature of the multinomial log-likelihood in `irls_update`. This method simply returns an array of ones so it is a no-op wherever a generic variance function might otherwise be referenced. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values (only used to determine output shape). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of ones with the same shape as `mu`. :::
